skill.name: python-best-practices
skill.description: Guides Python coding with type-first models, functional boundaries, structured errors, logging patterns, and optional type checker guidance.

security_audit.summary: Static analysis mostly matched Markdown fences and inline code, which are false positives in this documentation-only skill. One optional bash example shows uvx ty check, which is legitimate type-checking guidance but still requires user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: The optional uvx example can run an external package runner.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to ask before running uvx, and prefer project-pinned type checkers when available.

content.value_statement: Python projects often drift into weak typing, mutable models, and unclear error handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused rules for safer, clearer Python changes.
actual_capabilities: Recommends frozen dataclasses for immutable domain models.
Shows discriminated union patterns with Literal values.
Uses NewType for distinct domain identifiers.
Applies Protocol classes for structural typing.
Encourages exception chaining with preserved tracebacks.
Promotes module loggers and deferred log formatting.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not run analysis by itself.
It does not cover frameworks, packaging, or deployment workflows.
The type checker section references a rapidly evolving tool.
Examples are short and may need adaptation for large systems.

use_cases.title: Review Python Domain Models
use_cases.description: Check whether models use immutable data classes, precise identifiers, and type-safe state shapes.

use_cases.title: Improve Error Handling
use_cases.description: Refactor parsing and validation paths so exceptions preserve original context and report clear messages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Logging Style
use_cases.description: Align new Python modules with module-level loggers and deferred formatting for cleaner diagnostics.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Python File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python file using the python-best-practices skill. Focus on typing, errors, and logging. Suggest only practical changes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Domain Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these Python domain models using immutable data classes, NewType identifiers, and explicit state variants where helpful.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Error Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these parsing and validation functions for exception chaining, clear failure messages, and type-safe return states.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python module API that makes invalid states unrepresentable and uses Protocol boundaries for external dependencies.

output_examples.input: A mutable user model uses plain strings for every identifier.
output: Recommend an immutable data class for the user record.
Introduce distinct identifier types for user and order values.
Explain the type safety benefit in plain language.

output_examples.input: A parser catches a decoding error and raises a generic value error.
output: Keep the original exception as the cause of the new error.
Preserve a clear message for callers and logs.
Check whether the function should return an explicit success or failure state.

output_examples.input: A module prints debug messages while building application objects.
output: Replace print calls with a module-level logger.
Use deferred formatting for values included in log messages.
Keep log messages specific enough for troubleshooting.

best_practices: Prefer type-level distinctions for values that have different business meanings.
Preserve original exceptions when raising clearer application errors.
Use structured logger calls instead of direct output in application code.
anti_patterns: Do not model every domain identifier as an interchangeable string.
Do not replace detailed exceptions with generic errors that lose context.
Do not use eager string interpolation in debug log messages.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Python tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Any command execution depends on the agent and user approval.

faq.question: Which Python files does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Python source files and project configuration related to typing and code quality.

faq.question: Can it replace a type checker?
faq.answer: No. It helps write type-friendly code, but real projects still need automated type checking.

faq.question: Does it support framework-specific patterns?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on language-level Python patterns, not Django, FastAPI, or data science frameworks.

faq.question: Is the ty recommendation required?
faq.answer: No. The skill presents ty as an optional fast type checker, alongside pyright and mypy.

faq.question: Can Claude Code and Codex both use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
